question:
The value of the expression

\[\frac{(304)^5}{(29.7)(399)^4}\]

is closest to
solution:
The choices are widely separated, so bounds can identify the closest value without calculating the large powers exactly. Let
\[
E=\frac{304^5}{29.7\cdot399^4}.
\]
All the numbers are positive. Decreasing the numerator and increasing the denominator makes the fraction smaller, so
\[
E>\frac{300^5}{30\cdot400^4}
=10\left(\frac34\right)^4
=\frac{810}{256}>3.
\]
For an upper bound, notice that \(304<399\) and \(304<11\cdot29.7=326.7\). Therefore
\[
E=\frac{304}{29.7}\left(\frac{304}{399}\right)^4<11.
\]
Thus \(3<E<11\). Every listed value below \(3\) is farther from \(E\) than \(3\) is. Also, \(E\) is less than \(8\) away from \(3\), but more than \(19\) away from \(30\). The closest listed value is \(3\), choice D.

nodes.description: Evaluate expressions at specific values of their variables. Include expressions that arise from formulas used in real-world problems. nodes.label: 6.EE.A.2c

nodes.description: Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation, including problems where both decimal and scientific notation are used. Use scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities (e.g., use millimeters per year for seafloor spreading). Interpret scientific notation that has been generated by technology.
nodes.label: 8.EE.A.4

nodes.description: Explain patterns in the number of zeros of the product when multiplying a number by powers of 10, and explain patterns in the placement of the decimal point when a decimal is multiplied or divided by a power of 10. Use whole-number exponents to denote powers of 10.
nodes.label: 5.NBT.A.2

nodes.description: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions. For example, 3 2 × 3 –5 = 3 –3 = 1/3 3 = 1/27.
nodes.label: 8.EE.A.1

nodes.description: Solve multi-step real-life and mathematical problems posed with positive and negative rational numbers in any form ( whole numbers , fractions , and decimals), using tools strategically. Apply properties of operations to calculate with numbers in any form; convert between forms as appropriate; and assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies. For example: If a woman making $25 an hour gets a 10% raise, she will make an additional 1/10 of her salary an hour, or $2.50, for a new salary of $27.50. If you want to place a towel bar 9 3/4 inches long in the center of a door that is 27 1/2 inches wide, you will need to place the bar about 9 inches from each edge; this estimate can be used as a check on the exact computation.
nodes.label: 7.EE.B.3

edges.reason: Distribution or regrouping can shorten mixed arithmetic, but evaluating parentheses and following the operation order is a valid route without that simplification repertoire.
The additive stages of general four-operation signed expressions include signed sums and differences.
General four-operation expressions include division steps; the scope does not say every individual expression contains a divisor.
Computing powers and reasoning about their signs first requires the meaning of the exponent and base.
The mixed expressions include ordinary four-operation stages as well as powers, so their arithmetic remains a component.
The power subexpressions must be evaluated with the parity and sign rules before the remaining operations.
The negative-multiplier case uses the sign of signed products; only that arithmetic/sign component is required, not every multiplication exercise.
edges.scope: multiplying or dividing by negative numbers

edges.reason: The example illustrates an estimate, while the general purpose is not confined to summation. Approximate sums illustrate estimation but do not define all estimation tasks. A length estimate or a rough product estimate can teach the purpose without this addition procedure.
edges.scope: rounding-based approximate sums as one example
